updates.name: Gil Bohrer
updates.bio: Gil Bohrer is a Professor of Civil, Environmental and Geodetic Engineering at Ohio State, where he leads the Ecohydrology and Forest Meteorology Laboratory. He builds physical and empirical models of how organisms interact with atmospheric processes, bridging plant-scale function and regional scales, and runs meteorological and eddy-flux measurements in forests and wetlands.
updates.research_interests: Ecohydrology; environmental fluid dynamics; eddy flux measurements; evapotranspiration; greenhouse gas emissions and modeling; large-eddy simulations; wind dispersal and movement ecology; multi-scale modeling; wetlands and forests
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Civil, Environmental and Geodetic Engineering, The Ohio State University

updates.name: Gregory C. Johnson
updates.bio: Gregory C. Johnson is an oceanographer who served as an Oceanographer in NOAA PMEL's Ocean Climate Research Division from 1993 until April 2025 and has since been a PMEL Guest Scientist; he also holds an affiliate professorship at the University of Washington School of Oceanography. His work centres on Argo floats, repeat hydrography and global ocean climatologies.
updates.research_interests: Argo profiling floats; repeat hydrographic sections (U.S. CLIVAR/CO2 Repeat Hydrography, WOCE); global ocean mixed-layer and isopycnal climatologies (GOSML, MIMOC); abyssal and deep Southern Ocean warming and sea level rise; random-forest ocean heat mapping (RFROM); equatorial Pacific CTD/ADCP sections

updates.name: Grizelle Gonzalez
updates.bio: Grizelle González is Director of the USDA Forest Service International Institute of Tropical Forestry. Her publications listed on her Forest Service profile examine soil arthropod communities, litter decomposition and ecosystem responses to disturbances such as hurricanes, fire and canopy loss in tropical and subtropical forests.
updates.research_interests: Terrestrial ecology; tropical systems; soil biology; biogeochemistry

updates.name: Gustav Paulay
updates.bio: Gustav Paulay is Curator of Invertebrate Zoology at the Florida Museum of Natural History and an adjunct professor of biology, with a 1988 PhD from the University of Washington. He documents coastal marine biodiversity, chiefly on coral reefs and in the North Pacific, through large collaborative bioblitz surveys and studies how that diversity arose using paleontological, ecological and phylogenetic evidence.
updates.research_interests: Biogeography, evolution, systematics and natural history of marine invertebrates; marine biodiversity of tropical coral reefs and the North Pacific; marine speciation and species-distribution dynamics; large-scale marine biodiversity surveys (bioblitzes); island biology of Pacific islands

updates.name: H. Curtis Monger
updates.bio: H. Curtis Monger is Professor Emeritus in New Mexico State University's Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, where he taught pedology from 1992 to 2015, then led national soil survey standards for USDA-NRCS (2015-2021) before retiring. A pedologist, he studies desert soils, pedogenic carbonate and soil-geomorphology of the Chihuahuan Desert, including the Jornada Basin LTER.
updates.research_interests: Coupled geomorphic-biotic change; links between desert soils and the global carbon cycle; soil carbonate isotopes as paleoclimate records; geoarchaeology; soil-landscape evolution in the Chihuahuan Desert (Fort Bliss, Jornada LTER, Big Bend)
